== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|Myria is a village situated on flat, sandy plains between the city of [[Enosh]] and [[Damascan]] cities. The settlement is protected by wooden walls constructed from tied sticks, which serve to deter desert beasts and potential heretics. The interior of the village consists of a dense, maze-like collection of houses built from clay bricks or wood. While the land to its north is characterized by rocky terrain, hills, and small creeks, the area to its south is more fertile. Historically, Myria has been a site of significant conflict and destruction. The village was raided by soldiers and experienced intense combat between various [[Travelers]] and the [[Naraka Incarnation]], resulting in much of the settlement being reduced to ashes. Because of its proximity to [[Enosh]], it was suspected by some that the bloodline of [[Elysia]] might be found among its inhabitants. Despite being caught in the middle of larger political and supernatural struggles, Myria is considered a part of the kingdom.}}

== House of Blades ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-01-house-of-blades|Located on flat, sandy plains near a desert and the northwestern edge of the [[Latari Forest]], Myria is a village reachable by riding. The settlement is encircled by head-high wooden walls of sharp sticks and features a north gate, though it has suffered as scorched ruins. The surrounding rocky bluffs resemble the stone walls found in certain chambers, and the nearby [[Orgrith Cave]] is wide enough to hold half of the village's population. Myria serves as the origin for [[Alin]]'s party and was the intended destination for [[Simon]]'s group, representing a place to which people can be taken back.}}

== The Crimson Vault ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|Located near the [[Latari Forest]], Myria is a village protected by gates and watchmen. [[Alin]] once entered the settlement through the [[Naraka Gate]], where he used a simple cot, and [[Leah]] spent several years residing there. While [[Simon]] intended to liberate his friends from the village, he remained no different to [[Leah]] than he was to [[Alin]] or other locals. The village's history is marked by violence, having suffered raids by the [[Damascan army]] and an attack by an [[Endross Traveler]]. Ultimately, the sands of Myria became a battlefield where the [[Naraka Incarnation]] fought amidst the echoes of conflicts between [[Naraka creatures]] and residents of the [[City of Light]].}}
